title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1_C − {0,1,∞}, generated by loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with one product relation. Π̃_{0,3} = Π_{0,3}·{1,τ} is its extension by complex conjugation τ, with conjugation-type involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞. Π'_{0,3} is the oriented triangulated cartographic group Π_{0,3}/(l_1^2, l_∞^3), i.e. the orbifold π_1 of P^1 with signature (0, 2, 3) at (0,1,∞). Π̃'_{0,3} is its non-oriented version, the Coxeter-type group on σ_0, σ_1, σ_2 with relations (25).

The map (28). Π̃_{0,3} → Π̃'_{0,3}, sending τ_i to σ'_i, extends the quotient map (27).

The isomorphism (29). Grothendieck defines Π̃'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔊_{0,3}. Here 𝔊_{0,3} is (judging by the elements σ_∞, ρ, ε_i, λ_i = ε_i^2, σ_0, σ_1 on the next page) the full symmetry group of P^1−{0,1,∞}. This is the extension of S_3 × {1, conj} by Π_{0,3}, i.e. the orbifold π_1 of the quotient of P^1−{0,1,∞} by S_3 (and by conjugation). 𝔊^+_{0,3} is its orientation-preserving index-2 subgroup.
- The three generating involutions go to 'fundamental reflections' r_0 = τ'_∞ = σ_∞τ, r_1 = τ'_0 = σ_0τ, r_∞ = τ_∞.
- This restricts to (30): Π'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔊^+_{0,3}, with l'_0 ↦ ε_0 = σ_∞ρ, l'_1 ↦ σ_∞, l'_∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}.
- The NB records the products r_∞r_1 = l'_0, r_0r_∞ = l'_1, r_1r_0 = l'_∞.

Consequences.
- (31): 𝔊_{0,3} has the Coxeter presentation of the (2,3,∞) triangle group: r_i^2 = 1, (r_0r_∞)^2 = 1, (r_1r_0)^3 = 1, with r_∞r_1 of infinite order. This is PGL(2,Z).
- (32)/(33): 𝔊^+_{0,3} = ⟨σ_∞, ρ | σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL(2,Z).

In modern terms, the page identifies two incarnations of PSL(2,Z)/PGL(2,Z):
- the triangulated cartographic group, a quotient of Π_{0,3} (Esquisse, dessins d'enfants);
- the S_3-extended fundamental group of M_{0,4} = P^1−{0,1,∞}, in which Π_{0,3} sits with index 6, like Γ(2)/±1 in PSL(2,Z).

The next page realizes this concretely on the Poincaré half-plane, via reflections in the sides of the (i, e^{iπ/3}, ∞) triangle. This is preparatory bookkeeping for the 'équation des lacets' (the GT-type relations involving σ_∞, ρ, ε_i).
errors: No mathematical errors found; all relations check. (25) maps onto (31) correctly: σ_2σ_0 ↦ r_∞r_0 (order 2), σ_1σ_0 ↦ r_1r_0 (order 3). In (30), l'_0 = (l'_∞ l'_1)^{-1} = σ_∞ρ is consistent with l'_∞ l'_1 l'_0 = 1. The next page's formulas also verify: r_0r_∞(z) = −1/z, r_1r_0(z) = 1 − 1/z, r_∞r_1(z) = z − 1.
Notational clash: in the marginal note ρ is used as the name of the isomorphism, while in (30)-(33) ρ is the order-3 generator of 𝔊^+_{0,3}.

Minor: (28) writes Π̃_{0,3} → Π̃'_{0,3}, but only the restriction to Π_{0,3} was defined on the previous page; the extension is by definition via τ_i ↦ σ'_i, and compatibility is not checked explicitly.

ideas.what: The non-oriented triangulated cartographic group (generated by three involutions with (σ_2σ_0)^2 = (σ_1σ_0)^3 = 1) is identified with the (2,3,∞) Coxeter triangle group ≅ PGL(2,Z), and its oriented subgroup with PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2*Z/3.
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group as (2,3,∞) triangle group; cartographic groups of triangulated maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); cartographic setting by Grothendieck (Esquisse), with Jones–Singerman and Shabat–Voevodsky
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §3 on cartographic groups and triangulated maps

ideas.what: Isomorphism between the cartographic quotient Π_{0,3}/(l_1^2, l_∞^3) and the S_3 (and conjugation) extension 𝔊_{0,3} of Π_{0,3}, i.e. the orbifold π_1 of (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3. Elements σ_∞, ρ, ε_i, λ_i = ε_i^2 are made explicit.
ideas.modern_name: PSL(2,Z) ⊃ Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2 with quotient S_3; orbifold fundamental group of M_{0,4}/S_3 (≈ M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in the GT context Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the Longue Marche (1981) / Esquisse; not certain

ideas.what: Fundamental reflections r_0, r_1, r_∞ expressed as complex conjugation composed with S_3 symmetries (τ'_∞ = σ_∞τ, τ'_0 = σ_0τ), giving a Coxeter presentation of the real-structure-extended symmetry group.
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group / real structures on M_{0,4}; Coxeter presentation of PGL(2,Z)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard bookkeeping of PSL(2,Z)/PGL(2,Z) as cartographic, orbifold and triangle groups, consistent with what Grothendieck stated in the Esquisse and with classical modular-group theory. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The group symbol is fraktur 𝔊 (𝔊_{0,3}, 𝔊^+_{0,3}), not 𝔖 (symmetric group).

Margin note reads roughly: 'Cet iso. est uniquement déterminé par le fait qu'il induit un iso. ρ: Π'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔊^+_{0,3} ... i.e. Π̃'_{0,3} = Π'_{0,3}·{1,τ} ≅ 𝔊_{0,3}, 𝔊^+_{0,3} d'indice 2 dans 𝔊_{0,3} ... l'_1^2 = l'_∞^3 = 1'. These are primed objects (Π'), not Π_{0,3}.
Line after (28): 'Ceci posé, l'on définit un iso.' (the trailing 'en [?]' is a stray mark).
Annotations under (29) read 'sur τ'_∞ = σ_∞τ', 'sur τ'_0 = σ_0τ', 'sur τ', i.e. τ'_∞ = σ_∞τ, τ'_0 = σ_0τ.
The archive page number '90' at the bottom left is the archive foliation; the manuscript pagination runs 334→335 across this sheet.
